lines.text: We did hand signs all morning. My fingers are so tired they keep making the Tiger by themselves.
I can do the Clone now! Well, half a Clone. It came out lying down, but it's still a Clone.
Our instructor can tell who's talking even facing the board. I think there's a secret eye on the back of the head.
History is the worst. Who cares what happened a hundred years ago? It already happened!
I got a gold star for my shuriken throws. Three out of five on the post! The other two hit the fence.
Transformation is so hard. I tried to turn into a cat and I came out as me with whiskers.
We had a test on the twelve signs today. I mixed up the Hare and the Dog again. They look the same, I swear.
The library lady says if you read one scroll a week you'll be Chunin before anyone else. I've read two. Ever.
I sit by the window in class so I can watch the Genin squads walk past. That's learning too.
Practice kunai are blunt, but they still hurt if you drop one on your foot. Ask me how I know.
The janitor caught me drawing on the desk and made me scrub every desk in the room. I'm never drawing again. Until next week.
Our instructor makes us run laps if anyone's late. I'm never late. Somebody else always is.
I wrote my name on the inside of my practice headband so nobody steals it. Everybody's is the same, it's a problem.
My homework got rained on and now it looks like a frog sat on it. A frog did not sit on it. I'm pretty sure.
In the workshop today we made smoke bombs. Mine just made a sort of sad cough.
Substitution is the coolest. You get hit and then poof, it's a log! I can't do it yet, but I've got the poof part.
I made flashcards for all twelve signs. Rat, Ox, Tiger, Hare... do you want to borrow them? You have to give them back in order.
I counted. There are fourteen target posts in the yard, and one of them is shorter than the others. Nobody else noticed.
I'm going to be the best in the class by the end of the year. Maybe by the end of the week. I'm deciding.
Somebody said I throw like a duck. I'll show them. I'll throw like an angry duck.
I don't like it when the instructor calls on me. I know the answer, it just... hides when everyone looks.
I practise my hand signs under the desk where no one can see. I'm getting good at it. Don't tell.
I asked the instructor if you can do jutsu with your feet. I got sent to stand in the hall. It was a real question!
Did you know the target posts are made of cedar? I asked the carpenter. I ask the carpenter a lot of things.
At recess we play ninja and bandits. Nobody ever wants to be the bandit, so we just have a lot of ninja.
I'm the champion of the swing. I can go so high you can see over the Academy fence.
We played hide-and-seek and nobody found me for an hour. Then I realised nobody was looking.
Kick-the-can is the best game. The can is the Hokage and you have to protect it. Except we kick it.
I can climb the big tree out front to the third branch. The fourth branch is for Genin. I'll get there.
Tag is better with shinobi rules. If you do a hand sign before they tag you, it doesn't count.
We drew a map of the whole village in the dirt at recess. We put the ramen shop in the middle because it's the most important.
Shadow tag only works when it's sunny. On rainy days we just tag, which is worse.
The yard has a puddle that never dries. We call it the Lake of Doom. You have to jump over it or you lose.
We made up a jutsu called Thousand Pebbles. It's just throwing lots of pebbles, but it has a cool name.
Somebody brought a ball and we played until the bell. My team won. Probably. Nobody was counting right.
We had a race to the end of the yard and back. I came second, but the first one cheated with a running start.
You can play ninja and bandits with us at recess. You can even be a ninja. We have plenty of ninja.
Do you want to see my secret hiding spot? It's behind the woodshed. Well, it was secret.
Come and swing with me! I'll push you first, then you push me, and you have to push hard.
If you're on my team for kick-the-can, we'll win for sure. You look like a fast kicker.
The dango stall gives you an extra stick if you say please really nicely. You have to mean it, though.
My favourite snack is the sweet potato from the roasting cart. It burns your fingers but it's worth it.
I saved my lunch money all week to buy a whole bowl of ramen by myself. I'm going to eat every noodle.
Rice crackers are the best because they crunch so loud the instructor knows you're having a snack.
I traded my egg roll for a pickled plum. It was a bad trade. My whole face went inside out.
My grandma makes onigiri in the shape of animals. Today mine was a frog. I ate the eyes first.
The Akimichi kids always have the best lunches. They share sometimes, if you say nice things about the food.
Melon bread is my favourite. The bakery on the corner sells it warm if you're there before school.
I had three dango for breakfast. Don't tell my mum.
I like the pink dango best. The green one tastes like grass. Good grass, but still grass.
Somebody brought shaved ice with plum syrup to school and everybody crowded round. The ice melted before anybody got any.
I'm saving up for barbecue. It costs a lot more than ramen, but my cousin says it makes you punch harder.
My big sister is a Genin. She doesn't let me touch her kunai, but I touched it once when she was asleep.
My little brother keeps copying everything I do. I did a hand sign and he did it too, and then he fell over.
My dad works at the fish stall, so my lunch always smells like fish. I don't mind. The cats follow me everywhere.
My mum says I can't be a ninja and a baker at the same time. I'm going to be both and prove her wrong.
I've got four big brothers and every one of them was in the Academy. The instructors look at me like they're tired already.
My grandpa used to be a Chunin. He says when he was little the Academy was just a field and a stick.
My baby sister can't even talk yet, but I've been teaching her the Rat sign. She mostly grabs my nose.
My big brother says he'll teach me the Fireball when I'm older. He says that every time I ask, so I ask a lot.
My aunt runs the tea house on the corner. If I sweep the garden path, I get a free cup and a sweet bean cake.
My cousin is in the police. I asked if I could ride along and they said no, but they let me wear the hat once.
My parents both work at the market, so I walk home on my own. I'm very good at it. I only got lost twice.
My big sister snores so loud the neighbours knock on the wall. My mum says it's a family talent.
Nobody in my family is a ninja. We make tofu. But I'm going to be the first, and then the tofu will be famous.
My parents run a shop, so after the Academy I help count the stock. I can count to a thousand. In ryo, even.
I don't have a clan, but my mum says that just means I get to make up my own family technique. I'm calling it the Big Kick.
The clan kids get special jutsu. That's fine. I'm going to learn every normal jutsu twice as good.
I want a ninken so badly. The Inuzuka clinic has pups, and one of them licked my hand, so I think it picked me.
Our cat sleeps on my feet every night. I can't move my legs until morning, but I don't want to wake it.
There's a frog in the Academy pond that's bigger than my fist. We named it Hokage. It doesn't do anything, it just sits.
I fed the deer by the Nara forest. One of them ate my whole sleeve. My mum was not happy.
The ninken at the gate know my name. Well, they know the sound of my lunch box.
I found a beetle as big as a coin and showed it to an Aburame kid. They said it was a very good beetle. I was so proud.
Our neighbour's dog can do a trick where it rolls over and plays dead. I tried to teach it Substitution. It didn't work.
I want a cat from the shelter, but my dad says we already have enough with my brother.
There's a crow that sits on the Academy roof every day at lunch. I've been giving it rice. I think we're friends now.
The koi at the Hyuga estate are huge. I saw one through the gate. It looked at me like I was in trouble.
If I get a ninken, I'm going to name it Kunai. Or Ramen. Or Kunai Ramen.
A puppy from the kennels followed me all the way to the Academy. I had to walk it back. It was the best morning ever.
I touched the shrine bell at night on a dare. Nothing happened, but my heart is still going.
They dared me to run past the Uchiha gate shouting. I made it halfway and then a grown-up looked at me.
The biggest dare is climbing to the second Hokage's eyebrow. Nobody has ever done it. Nobody has even tried really.
I ate a whole raw onion on a dare. I won, but now my mouth is a battlefield.
Somebody dared me to put my feet in the river in winter. I did it for a count of ten. I'm still cold.
The best dare is sneaking into the training grounds after dark. I got as far as the first stump and a frog jumped on me.
I bet the new kid can't do a cartwheel off the Academy steps. I did one. I kind of landed on my face.
They dared me to knock on the Shimura door and run. I knocked, but I was too scared to run, so I just stood there.
I climbed the water tank on our roof on a dare. I could see all the way to the wall! Then I couldn't get down.
Daring someone to sit alone in the hospital waiting room after dark is the scariest dare. I don't do that one.
I dare you to jump across the Lake of Doom in the yard! Run-up allowed!
Bet you can't stand on one leg longer than me. Ready? Go! Hey, that's cheating, you can't use chakra!
I saw a Genin walk across the river today. Across it! On top! I'm going to practise in the bath tonight.
There's a Chunin on my street who can jump from one roof to the next without even looking. I want to do that.
When a squad comes back through the gate, I wave at them. Sometimes they wave back. Once a Jonin did.
Genin get real missions! I would do any mission. Even the cat ones. Especially the cat ones.
The Genin at the training grounds threw shuriken so fast I couldn't even see them. Then they hit a stump, thunk-thunk-thunk.
My hero is the Jonin who lives above the tofu shop. They bought me a dango once and didn't even ask for anything.
The Hokage's guard stands so still I thought they were statues. Then one sneezed.
I want to get my headband so badly. I practise tying it on with my old scarf every night.
A Genin squad was eating at Ichiraku and I sat next to them. They talked about a mission with a goat. A goat!
When I graduate I'm going to the Mission Desk first thing. I'll take the hardest D-rank they have.
The flak vests the Chunin wear have so many pockets. I bet there's a snack in at least one of them.
I followed a Genin home to see where they live. They noticed and gave me a lecture. It was so cool.
You're a real Genin! Can I touch your headband? Just the edge. I won't smudge it.
Is it true Genin get to go outside the wall? What's out there? Are there bears? Are there big bears?
Show me a jutsu, please! Even a little one! I won't tell anyone, I promise. Well, I'll tell a few people.
I want to see the Hokage up close. I stood outside the Residence all morning and only saw a hawk.
I'm going to be Hokage one day, and my face will be on the Rock, and it's going to be smiling.
My grandpa says he shook a Hokage's hand once. He hasn't washed it since. That was forty years ago. Gross.
If you climb to the top of the Rock you can sit on the Hokage's heads. I haven't done it. I'm working up to it.
The Hokage works in the round building. My friend says there's a slide inside. I don't think there's a slide.
I drew all the Hokage faces in my notebook. The third one came out looking like my dad.
Do you think the Hokage ever eats ramen? I hope so. Everybody should.
When I'm Hokage I'm going to make it a rule that every day ends with dango.
I don't like the hospital. It smells like soap and medicine and everyone talks in whispers.
I had to get a splinter out at the hospital. The medic was really nice, but the tweezers were the size of a kunai.
My big brother stayed in the hospital for a week after a mission. I brought him a drawing of a frog. He kept it on his bed.
The hospital has a room with painted frogs on the walls. That's the room for kids. It's still scary.
I heard if you get hurt in training they take you to the hospital and give you the worst porridge in the world. I'm never getting hurt.
I'm scared of the dark lanes by the wall at night. My mum says the Tobari are watching, so it's safe. That doesn't help.
Thunder used to scare me. Now I just count. If I get to ten before it bangs, it's far away.
The instructor says even Jonin get scared. I don't believe that. Maybe a little. Maybe Jonin are scared of the hospital too.
I get scared before tests. My stomach goes all wobbly. Then I eat a rice ball and it's a bit better.
I don't like loud noises. The forge on the market street makes my ears ring, so I walk past it really fast.
I've been training my secret jutsu. It's called Silent Stomp. You stomp, but quietly.
When I grow up I'm going to have a summon. It'll be a giant cat. My mum says we don't have room.
I made a headband out of my mum's old belt. It has a leaf drawn on it in ink. It's almost real.
I've been sneaking up on my brother all week. I'm getting so good he didn't even know until I sneezed.
I practise tree walking on the tree in our garden. I get two steps up and then I'm on my back again.
I tied a rope between two chairs and practised walking on it like a ninja. Then the chairs fell over.
I'm going to invent a jutsu that makes vegetables taste like dango. Everyone will want me on their squad.
I hid in a cupboard for an hour pretending it was a mission. I learned the cupboard is very boring and very dusty.
Sometimes I pretend the main street is the Forest of Death and the shoppers are enemy ninja. I've never been caught.
I want to go outside the wall and see the whole world. And then come back for dinner.
My friends and I have a squad. We even have a name. We're not telling anyone the name.
I made my own sealing tag with a brush and some rice paper. It doesn't seal anything, but it looks great on my door.
Do you want to be in my squad? We need someone who can throw. Or run. Or just be good at hiding.
We should practise hand signs together after the Academy. You do one, I copy it, then I do one and you copy it.
When we both make Genin, let's eat at Ichiraku together. I'm going to order the biggest bowl.
You're pretty good at the Academy stuff. Can you show me how you do the Ram? Mine looks like a sock puppet.
I jumped in every puddle from my house to the Academy. My sandals are full of water, but I won.
When it rains the frogs in the Academy pond sing so loud you can't hear the instructor. Best days ever.
We're building a snow Hokage outside the Academy! It's got a big hat and stick arms and a scary face.
I tried to catch snowflakes on my tongue and caught a leaf instead. It tasted like a leaf.
Did you hear that thunder? I wasn't scared. I just jumped because my foot slipped.
Summer means the river! We go to the shallows after lessons and try to catch fish with our hands. Nobody's caught one yet.
I'm collecting the reddest maple leaves in the village. I've got thirty. I'm pressing them in my history scroll.
The cherry blossoms are out! I caught a petal before it hit the ground, so I get a wish. I wished for a ninken.
My mum knitted me a scarf so long I can wrap it round three times. I'm going to use it as a rope for ninja training.
There's a cat on our street that keeps stealing socks. It's got a whole pile of them under the tea house porch.
Somebody keeps leaving a rice ball at the little shrine on the corner every morning. I've been trying to catch who, but I always fall asleep.
I lost my lucky marble somewhere by the river. It's blue with a white swirl. If you find it, it's mine.
My friend says there's a secret tunnel under the Academy. I think it's just a cellar, but I still want to see it.
The old grandma at the end of our lane gives a sweet to anyone who carries her shopping. I've carried it four times this week.
The bath house has a mural of the Hokage Rock on the wall. Somebody painted a moustache on one face and they never got it all off.
I know every shortcut from my house to the Academy. There are eleven. Twelve if you can climb a fence.
There's a dango stall by the shrine steps that only opens on festival days. That's my favourite stall in the whole world.
The fish stall man gives me the fish heads for our cat. The cat loves them. I don't look at them.
On Market Day I help my parents carry baskets. The best part is the free sample from the pickle stall. The worst part is the pickle.
The ramen shop has a stool that wobbles. I always pick that one. It's like a ride.
The lanterns on the main street go on all at once at dusk. I try to blink at the exact second. I never get it.
The training grounds are way bigger than they look from the Rock. I walked to the third stump and my legs fell off. Not really.
At the festival there's a game where you catch goldfish with a paper scoop. I've never caught one. The paper always breaks.
My street has a cobbler who can fix any sandal. I brought in my practice headband once, and that got fixed too.
I brought two rice balls today in case somebody forgot theirs. Somebody always forgets theirs.
My grandma has a cold, so I'm making her soup after school. I'm only allowed to stir, but stirring is the important part.
The new kid in our class sat alone at lunch, so I sat there too. Now we both sit there. It's a good spot.
I gave my umbrella to a little kid in the rain and walked home wet. My mum was cross but she also gave me a hug.
When the instructor looks tired I clean the board before anyone asks. The chalk dust makes me sneeze, but it's worth it.
I keep a sweet in my pocket for whoever cries at recess. Today it was me, so I ate it myself.
The stray cat by the tea house looked hungry, so I shared my fish. Now it waits for me every day.
I made a get-well card for a Genin in the hospital. I don't know them, but nobody should be in the hospital without a card.
I always save the last dango on the stick for my little brother. He doesn't know it's the best one.
If you're tired you can lean on me. I'm small but I'm very sturdy.
I knitted a scarf for my dad. It has three holes and one sleeve by accident, but he wears it anyway.
Our neighbour lives on their own, so I bring the newspaper up every morning. They give me a pickled plum. I don't like pickled plums, but I like the visit.
I'm going to be a medic ninja so I can fix everybody. I've already practised bandaging my teddy fourteen times.
Did you eat breakfast? You look like you didn't eat breakfast. Here, have half my melon bread.
Why do we need twelve hand signs? Why not ten? I asked, and the instructor said good question, which means nobody knows.
I read that the Hokage Rock took a whole season to carve each face. That's a lot of chipping. I wonder if anyone sneezed and ruined a nose.
I think clouds are like jutsu. They change shape when you're not looking, and nobody can tell you the signs.
If a Clone sees another Clone, does it know which one is real? I've been thinking about it for three days.
I like the library because nobody shouts there. You can hear your own thoughts. Mine are quite loud.
The instructor says history repeats itself. So I'm learning it twice, to be safe.
I counted the steps up to the shrine. Two hundred and one. Everyone says two hundred, but I counted twice.
Do you think the fish in the river know about the village? They must hear us all day.
I don't want to be the strongest. I want to be the one who knows what to do. That's different.
My grandpa says every scroll in the library was written by someone who was once a kid like us. I keep thinking about that.
I watched the ants carrying crumbs across the yard. They're very organised. They'd make a good squad.
I asked why the Uchiha live at the edge of the village. My mum said it's a long story. All the good things are long stories.
Before I go to sleep, I go through all the hand signs in my head. It's better than counting sheep.
When I'm older I'll write a scroll about everything the instructors forgot to tell us. It will be very long.
I put a frog in the instructor's desk drawer. Well, I opened the drawer and the frog got in. That's different.
Want to hear a joke? Why did the shuriken go to school? To get sharper! Ha! I made that up just now. Well, this morning.
I can make a face like the third Hokage on the Rock. Look. No, look properly. That's it, that's the face.
I hid my friend's sandals on the Academy roof. Then I couldn't get them back down. So it was kind of a joke on me.
Tag, you're it! No, wait, I'm not playing yet. Okay, now. Tag!
I've been practising walking backwards everywhere. I've bumped into four people and one stall. My backwards is getting good.
I drew a moustache on my own face in ink so the instructor would think I was a Jonin in disguise. It didn't work.
I can whistle with my fingers. Listen! The dogs at the kennels heard that. Every single dog.
We swapped headbands with the class next door at recess. Nobody noticed until roll call. It was the best roll call ever.
I'm the best at making everyone laugh during the quiet time. I'm also the best at standing in the hall.
I taught the crow on the roof to steal rice crackers. It's a very good student. Too good.
Guess which hand the pebble's in! Wrong! It was in my sandal the whole time.
If I could do any jutsu, I'd make one that turns the instructor's chalk into dango. Every lesson would be delicious.
Let's see who can hop on one foot all the way to the ramen shop. Loser pays! I only have two ryo, so please don't win.
I want to see what's past the hills outside the wall. I bet there's a mountain made of ice. Or a lake as big as the village.
I followed the river all the way to the wall grate yesterday. It keeps going on the other side! I wanted to keep going too.
When I'm a Genin I'm taking every mission that goes far away. The further, the better. Even the boring ones, if they're far.
I climbed the tallest tree by the training grounds. I could see the gate and the road going out forever.
There's a cave behind the Nara forest that my cousin found. Well, it's more of a hole. A big hole. It's still exciting.
My uncle is a merchant and he's been to the coast. He says the sea tastes like salt soup. I need to taste it myself.
I keep a bag packed under my bed. Rice cracker, rope, a candle and my lucky stone. In case adventure happens at night.
The travellers at the gate have the best stories. I sit by the booth and listen until the guards tell me to go home.
I made a map of the village with a big blank bit where outside the wall is. I'm going to fill it in one day.
Someday I'll go to every village there is, and eat their ramen, and come home and tell Ichiraku who does it best.
I walked on top of the garden wall from our house to the end of the lane. That's practically a mission.
The Forest of Death is the scariest place in the world and I want to go in it more than anything. When I'm allowed.
I asked a Jonin what's the farthest they've been. They said, far enough to miss home. I want to go that far.
Let's explore the old lane behind the bath house after school! I heard there's a staircase that goes nowhere.
My pencil case has a slot for every pencil. If one's missing, I know which one. It's always the red one.
I fold my practice headband exactly the same way every night. Three folds, then a tuck. It looks perfect in the morning.
I made a chart of every snack at the dango stall and how much each costs. The green ones went up by a ryo. I noticed.
The instructor wrote the Tiger sign wrong on the board today. Just a little wrong. I fixed it at lunch when nobody was looking.
My handwriting is the neatest in the class. I practise one character a hundred times until it stops wobbling.
I lined up my shuriken by size before practice. Then the wind blew them over. I had to start again.
My lunch box has three compartments, and the food is not allowed to touch. Rice is rice. Fish is fish.
I keep a notebook of every time I hit the target post. Forty-one hits this month. Last month was thirty-eight. Progress.
Our classroom clock is two minutes slow. I told the instructor. The instructor said thank you very slowly.
I sweep my room every morning before the Academy. My brother says I'm strange. My room says I'm right.
I learned the hand signs in order, then backwards, then in pairs. Now I'm learning them in alphabetical order.
If you fold your scroll the wrong way it gets a crease forever. Please don't borrow mine.
I timed how long it takes to walk to the Academy. Eight minutes on a normal day, eleven on Market Day.
The rows in the yard are crooked when we line up. I always stand where the line should be. Nobody else does.
I promised my mum I'd be home before the lanterns. I've never been late once. Not once.
I practise my throws every morning, even when it's raining. Especially when it's raining. Real missions don't wait for sun.
I'm not the best in class, but I'm always there. The instructor says that counts for a lot.
My friend dropped a practice kunai down the well and I helped fish it out. Took all afternoon. We got it.
If I say I'll help you, I'll help you. That's just how it is.
I carry my grandpa's shopping up the stairs every Market Day. Forty-two stairs. My legs are very strong now.
I didn't get the Clone right today. Or yesterday. I'll get it tomorrow, or the day after. I'm not stopping.
My big sister says I'm stubborn. I say I'm steady. We say it at the same time, and then we laugh.
The whole class gave up on running laps, but I finished mine. Slowly. Still finished.
I've been feeding the cat by the tea house every day for a year. It's my job now. I take it seriously.
When the instructor needs someone to carry the target posts, I put my hand up first. Somebody has to.
I keep my word. Even when it's about something small, like returning a pencil.
I don't cry when I fall. I get up. Sometimes I cry later, at home, but that doesn't count.
If you need a partner for practice, I'll be one. I'm not fancy, but I don't give up.
I like the corner of the library. It's quiet. Nobody asks me things there.
Hm. The dango's good today.
I don't talk much at recess. I watch. I know who's winning before they do.
My favourite place is the bench behind the woodshed. Nobody goes there. Except you, now.
I have one friend. That's enough.
The noise in the yard is a lot. I sit by the tree until the bell.
I can do the Clone. I just don't show anyone.
You don't have to talk. We can just sit. That's fine.
I like rain. Fewer people outside.
I drew a picture of the Hokage Rock. It's in my bag. I'm not showing it. Maybe later.
My mum says I'm like a cat. I come out when I want to.
Everyone was shouting about the Genin squad. I just looked. They looked tired.
I said hello to the instructor today. Out loud. That was a lot.
Thanks for not making me talk. Most people do.
If the Hokage Rock could talk, I bet the faces would argue about who has the best nose all night.
The clouds today look like a giant ninken chasing a bowl of ramen across the sky. Look, there's the noodle!
I dreamt the Academy was a boat and we sailed it down the river to the sea. The instructor was the captain and had a parrot.
My shadow is my secret twin. When I go to sleep it goes out and does missions. That's why I'm always tired.
I named every stone on the path to the Academy. The round one is called Grandpa Pebble. He's very wise.
What if the lanterns on the main street are tiny suns that come out at night because they're shy in the day?
I made up a whole village under the floor of our house. Tiny ninja ride beetles there. They're at war with the mice.
The river sounds like it's whispering secrets. Mostly about fish, I think.
If I could paint the sky, I'd make it orange with purple stripes, and every cloud would be a different flavour.
The big tree at the Academy is really an old giant who fell asleep standing up. The swing is its earring.
I'm writing a story about a frog who becomes Hokage. It's twenty pages. The frog hasn't even left the pond yet.
When it snows, I pretend the village is a huge rice cake and I'm a sesame seed walking across it.
My scarf is actually a dragon that's asleep. When I need it, it'll wake up. For now it's just warm.
The forge on the market street is a cave where a fire monster lives. The smith feeds it every morning.
I sell my extra rice crackers at recess for a ryo each. I'm saving for a real kunai. Forty ryo. I'm at twelve.
Hand signs are useful, but carrying the lunch basket gets you extra snacks. You have to think about what matters.
Why run to the Academy when you can walk fast? Same time, less sweat.
My mum gives me five ryo a week. Three for dango, two saved. By winter I'll have a lot.
I don't trade my egg roll for anything less than a whole pickle. That's the rule.
Practice shuriken are cheap, so I practise with those. When I get good, then I'll spend money on the real ones.
The cheapest lunch in the village is the Academy rice balls. Two ryo. I know all the prices.
If you sweep the tea house path, you get a free cup and a cake. That's worth more than two ryo. Good deal.
I don't need to be the best thrower. I just need to hit what I'm aiming at. That's different, and it's cheaper.
My brother wastes his pocket money on paper fans. I'm saving mine for a pet. Pets are useful. Fans are not.
Before the test I studied the stuff that's always on the test. Smart, not hard.
You should always bring an extra pair of socks. Puddles happen. I'm the only one with dry feet today.
I helped the grocer stack crates and got paid in apples. Apples are just ryo you can eat.
When I'm a Genin I'll do every D-rank they have. Cat missions pay the same as fence missions and cats are easier.
How does the water get into the round tanks on the roofs? Does somebody climb up with a bucket? Every day?
Why do the Aburame wear glasses? Can bugs see through them? Can they see the bugs?
I asked the smith how kunai are made and got to watch the whole thing. It was so loud. I want to watch again.
Where does the river go after the wall? Does it end? Can a river end?
I heard the Hokage Residence has a room full of nothing but scrolls. What's in them? I want to read all of them.
What makes ramen broth so good? I asked the cook and they just laughed. That means it's a secret, right?
Do you know why the Hyuga bow so many different ways? I tried to count them and lost count.
How do Genin water-walk? Is it the same as tree walking but wetter? I'm going to find out.
I asked the gate guard what's in the big book. Names! Every visitor ever! I want to read it, but I'm not allowed.
How do the hawks at the Residence know where to fly? Do they have tiny maps? I bet they have tiny maps.
Where do the stray cats go at night? I followed one and it went up a wall. I can't go up walls yet.
Why are the Hokage faces carved and not painted? Painting would be faster. I asked three grown-ups and got three answers.
What does chakra feel like when you have a lot of it? Is it tingly? Mine just feels like being hungry.
I found a little door at the bottom of the Academy wall. What's it for? Nobody will tell me.
If anyone's mean to my little sister at recess, they have to deal with me. I'm small, but I'm very loud.
I walk my friend home past the dark lane every day. Nobody's ever done anything there, but you never know.
When we play ninja and bandits, I'm always the one guarding the base. Somebody has to.
A big kid pushed the new kid in the yard. I stood in the way. The big kid left. I was shaking, but I did it.
I check the stray kittens under the tea house every morning to make sure they're all still there. Five today. Good.
Don't climb the water tank, it's slippery. I'm not being bossy, I'm being careful.
When I'm a ninja I'm going to guard the gate so nothing bad ever gets in. Not even a mosquito.
My brother's scared of thunder, so I sit with him during storms. I tell him it's just the sky practising.
If you get hurt during practice, tell me. I've got a bandage in my bag. Two, actually.
I always count everybody when we go on a school walk. The instructor does too, but I double-check.
The little kids in the lower class look up to us, so I try to be good in front of them. Mostly.
I don't like it when people go into the river alone. Come with someone. Come with me.
My grandpa walks with a stick, so I carry his shopping and watch for wobbly cobbles.
You can stand behind me if the dogs at the kennels bark too much. They're friendly. Mostly.
I found a baby bird that fell out of its nest. I put it back very gently. I hope its mum didn't mind.
I like quiet mornings when the dew is on the grass and the yard is empty. It feels like the world is still sleeping.
The deer at the Nara forest let me pat them if I'm very slow. You have to be slower than slow.
I don't like throwing things at the target posts. It feels mean, even though they're just wood.
I picked some wildflowers for the instructor's desk. They were a bit squashed, but the instructor smiled.
I sing to the cat by the tea house. Very quietly. It purrs. I think it likes my singing.
When somebody cries at recess I sit next to them. I don't say anything. Sometimes that's enough.
I want to be a medic or a gardener. Something where you make things better.
My little cousin is afraid of the dark, so I made a paper lantern with a smiling face on it.
I share my lunch with the crow on the roof. It's not a nice crow, but it's hungry.
I'm not very good at sparring. I always say sorry when I hit someone. The instructor says I don't have to.
The flowers at the Yamanaka shop smell like spring even in winter. I go in just to smell them.
I keep the worms off the path after rain so nobody steps on them. It takes a long time.
You look a bit sad today. Would you like to see the kittens with me? They make everything better.
I got the best mark on the hand sign test. Again. I'm not bragging, I'm just reporting facts.
My family has been in the village since the beginning. Well, nearly the beginning. Close enough.
I can throw a shuriken further than anybody in my class. I measured. With a rope.
My headband is the shiniest in the class because I polish it every night. Presentation matters.
I don't need help with my homework. I need a harder homework.
The instructor asked me to show the class the Clone. Of course they did. Who else would they ask?
I'm not going to be just any Genin. I'm going to be a Genin people talk about.
My grandma says I walk like a Jonin already. She's right. Look at this walk.
Somebody beat me in the race today. Fine. Tomorrow they won't. I'm practising my start tonight.
I wear my sandals the proper way, laced tight. Sloppy sandals are for sloppy ninja.
My brother is a Chunin. I'm going to be a Chunin faster than he was. He knows. He's worried.
I don't like losing. I don't mind it, I just don't like it. There's a difference.
I've been practising my bow. It's very elegant. The Hyuga kids even noticed.
Everyone wants to sit next to me at lunch. I let them, sometimes. I'm generous like that.
I'm going to be Hokage! And not one of the boring ones! The best one ever!
I ran so fast at recess I tripped over my own feet. I'll run faster next time, so fast my feet can't catch up!
Somebody said I couldn't do the Clone by the end of the week. Watch me! I'm going to do it by Fourth Day!
I ate three bowls of ramen yesterday! I'm going to eat four today! My stomach is ready!
The instructor told me to calm down. I'm calm! This is calm! I'm being very calm right now!
I challenged the biggest kid to a race and lost. I'm going to challenge them again every day until I win!
When I see a Genin squad I want to shout HELLO as loud as possible. So I do!
I'm going to train until my hands fall off! Then I'll train with my feet!
I hate waiting! Why does the Academy take a whole year? I could be a Genin tomorrow!
I tried to do a Fireball like my cousin and just breathed out really hard. I'm still counting it!
Thunderstorms are amazing! Every crash makes me want to yell back at the sky!
I'm not mad, I'm determined! There's a difference! It's louder!
Someone took the last melon bread! The last one! I'm going to be there earlier tomorrow, at dawn!
Let's spar right now! Right here! Okay, maybe after lunch. But then right away!
Um. Hi. I just... wanted to say hi. That's all.
I made you a... no, never mind. It's nothing. It's a paper crane. You can have it.
I didn't put my hand up even though I knew the answer. I'll try tomorrow. Maybe.
The instructor said my throw was good. Nobody else heard. That's okay. I heard.
I like sitting at the back. You can see everybody, and nobody looks at you.
I wanted to play kick-the-can but I didn't know how to ask. I just watched. It looked fun.
I talked to a Genin today! Well, I said "excuse me". But they said "sure"! That counts, doesn't it?
Sorry, I'm in the way. I'll move. No, it's... you can have the swing.
My voice goes small when I'm nervous. It's small a lot.
I practise saying hello to the cat by the tea house. It doesn't laugh at me.
I'm better at hand signs when nobody's watching. Could you... not watch? Thanks.
I wrote a poem about the Hokage Rock. It's... it's not very good. You can read it if you want. Later.
I got through a whole lunch talking to the new kid. My cheeks were red, but I did it.
If you want, we could... walk home the same way. Only if you want.
Stop running in the corridor. It's not allowed. I'm not the instructor, but I know the rules.
You did the Ram wrong. Fingers straight. Again. Better.
I practise every morning for an hour. If you want to be good, so should you.
Recess is for practice, not for messing about. That's what I think. Nobody agrees, but they're wrong.
My grandpa was a Jonin. He says discipline is the first jutsu. I'm working on it.
Tie your headband properly. A loose headband is a loose mind.
I don't laugh at the class clown's jokes. It only encourages them.
If you're going to throw, throw properly. Feet apart. Eyes on the target. No, the other target.
I finished my homework before dinner. Every night. It's not hard; you just have to start.
Don't eat dango before practice. You'll be slow. Eat after. That's the reward.
The little kids look at us. Behave. They'll copy everything.
I was late once. Once. I still think about it.
You want to be a ninja? Then stop yawning in the lesson. I saw that.
Good throw. That's all I'll say. Don't get comfortable.
There's a tree growing right through the middle of our hall. When it rains the roof drips into bowls and it sounds like music.
I planted my sapling on clan day. It's only as tall as my knee, but it already has six leaves. I count them every morning.
My grandma makes me water the big tree before breakfast. The tree drinks first, then me. That's the rule.
Guests at our house always get tea under the tree. I'm allowed to carry the cups now. I've only dropped one.
Our hall has masks all over the walls. They're a bit scary at night, but my auntie says they're family.
Every spring we paint the seals on the memorial. I got to hold the ink pot this year. I didn't spill any. Hardly any.
There aren't many of us, so clan day is one big table. I sit right next to the oldest one, who tells the best stories.
I can draw a spiral perfectly now. I practised a hundred times. It's our family's shape.
There's a fan painted on everything in our quarter. Even my lunch box. Even my socks, if you look closely.
My cousin is in the police. They have a real station with lanterns that never go out. I'm going to join when I'm sixteen.
At the police parade I got to carry a paper fan and march. I was out of step the whole time, but I marched hard.
We live right at the edge of the village. It takes forever to walk to the Academy, so I'm the fastest walker in class.
At home we have to bow differently to everybody. I mixed up two of them yesterday and my uncle went very quiet.
The koi in our pond are enormous. The white one is the oldest and it sulks if you're late with the food. Like my grandpa.
Tea at home is very quiet. Nobody's allowed to talk until the grown-up talks first. Sometimes nobody talks at all.
My cousins and I spar after dinner. That's how we settle arguments. I'm winning more arguments lately.
Everyone at my house plays shogi on the porch. I can beat my little sister. Nobody else yet.
We have a whole forest of deer behind our house. I helped count them last year. They kept moving, so I counted some twice.
My dad lies on the grass and watches clouds for hours. He says it's thinking. Mum says it's napping. I'm not sure.
In spring I collect the antlers the deer drop. I found eleven this year. That's my record.
Dinner at our house is forty people. You have to eat fast or it's gone. That's why I'm the fastest eater in class.
We always lay out one extra bowl at dinner in case somebody turns up. Somebody always turns up.
I'm learning to turn meat at the barbecue house. My uncle says I'm a natural. I've only burned three pieces.
At our house you have to eat the third helping. It's a rule. I love this rule.
Our house is the flower shop on the main street. I'm allowed to water the front buckets every morning.
Every flower means something. Yellow chrysanthemums mean something sad, so I never give those to anyone.
There's a greenhouse behind our shop that's warm even in winter. I go in there to do my homework when it snows.
On clan day we make a big garland with a flower from everyone. I picked a daisy this year. It's at the very end.
On clan day I sat in the circle and a puppy climbed right into my lap. That's my partner now. Its name is Pebble.
Our house is louder than the whole market. Forty dogs and my grandma, and my grandma is the loudest.
I sleep in a pile with my pup every night. My feet are always warm, and my face is always licked.
We race the Aburame kids in the outer fields every year. The dogs always win. The bugs say it doesn't count.
At our house every guest gets a seat by the fire, even in summer. I sit on the floor so there's room.
There's a monkey painted on our gate. My big brother says it used to be scary. Now it looks like it's smiling.
At New Year we lead the lantern walk. I got my own lantern this year. I held it so carefully it didn't even flicker.
Our yard is black from fire training. Nothing grows there. I like drawing on the ground with a stick, and it comes out grey.
Our house hums at night because of the hives. I can't sleep anywhere else. It's too quiet.
Rule one at home: never swat anything. I've never swatted a fly in my life. Not even a mosquito. It was hard.
On insect night the fireflies all come up at once from the garden. It's the best night of the year.
I have a beetle collection. I don't keep them in jars, I just know where they all live. That's better.
Our house is really big and really quiet. The old dogs sleep on the porch all afternoon.
The dogs at home decide who they like. They liked my friend straight away. They don't like the postman.
There are lots of empty rooms at our house. I play ninja in all of them. Each one is a different mission.
We have a bucket in the study because the roof drips. The bucket has a name. I named it.
Everyone at my house paints. Even breakfast is messy. I had ink on my rice this morning.
My aunt painted a screen of a crane and I swear it moved its head. My aunt says I imagined it. My aunt is smiling.
We're not allowed to finish painting an eye when people are watching. I always cover my picture with my arm.
There's an exhibition every autumn. This year one of my drawings is going up. It's a pear. It took four tries.
At home we don't talk at dinner. It's not because anyone's cross. It's just how we do it.
Our garden is three stones and some gravel. I tried to put a flower in it and got a very long look.
My grandpa says silence is polite. I'm practising being very polite at the Academy. The instructor likes it.
Our house is right under the Rock. In the afternoon the shadow of the faces covers our roof and everything goes cool.
Our house is in a grove of really old trees. I climb the split one on clan day. Only family gets to sit inside it.
There are roses all over our gate, with big thorns. I've got scratches on both arms from picking one for my mum.
At the grove viewing, guests drink tea that might not be tea. I know the trick but I'm not allowed to tell.
I like the grove in the mist. You can't tell which trees are real. Even I can't sometimes.
There's a platform on our dojo roof for looking at the moon. I'm allowed to stay up there on full moons.
My family does sword practice before breakfast. I only have a wooden one, but I do it every morning.
There's a crescent worn in our dojo floor from everybody standing in it. I stood in it on clan day. It fits my feet perfectly.
Swords at my house all have names. When I get mine I'm calling it Moonbeam. Or maybe something scarier.
Our house has a wall full of targets out front. I'm only allowed to throw at the bottom row. For now.
My dad keeps a senbon in his mouth all the time. I tried it with a chopstick and got told off.
Clan day is a throwing contest at the barracks. I came fourth in the little kids. Fourth out of five, but still.
The guards from the barracks eat dinner at our house sometimes. They let me try on their vests. They're heavy.
Our house has bars on the windows, but my grandma grows violets on them. It's the prettiest house on the street.
My mum wears a big long coat to work. At home she makes the best pancakes in the village.
On clan day nobody's allowed to ask questions at dinner. I tried to last the whole night and asked about pudding.
We have canaries at home. Three of them. I'm allowed to feed them, and they sing when I come in.
Everybody in my family is a teacher. Even dinner is a lesson. Last night was fractions with tofu.
Our house is right by the Academy. I can hear the roll call from my bed. I'm never late. I can't be late.
On teachers' day, old pupils leave notes on our step. One said thank you for the hard sums. I thought that was funny.
There's always marking on our table. I do my homework in the gaps.
Our shop is the one with the pink awning. After the Academy I help count the stock. I'm very fast.
At the anniversary sale we give away sweets to the whole street. I'm in charge of the sweet basket. I eat one per hour.
There's a cherry tree in our garden that's as old as the shop. In spring our whole house is pink.
I can count change faster than my big brother, and he's a Genin. He says that's not a ninja skill. It is to me.
Every morning we cross the river on the stepping stones. I fell in nine times this year. Only nine!
In our dojo you have to take your sandals off. The floor is so shiny you can see yourself.
On clan day whoever splashes first serves dinner. I've served dinner every year. One day it won't be me.
My grandpa can walk across a room full of dry leaves and not make a sound. I sound like a whole cart.
My family guards the gate. My auntie knows every cart by the sound of its wheels. I'm learning.
We have a shop next to the forge, so our house smells like metal. I like it. It smells like home.
On clan day everybody hammers a nail into the beam over our door. I hammered mine in crooked. It's still there.
Everyone at our house tells stories from the gate at dinner. I tell stories from the Academy. Mine are better.
My family builds houses. Our yard smells like cedar, and there are shavings in my hair every single day.
I built my first stool! It wobbles a bit, but my dad put it in the yard where everyone can see it.
On clan day we put a whole roof on a house in one day. I carried the nails. Hundreds of nails.
I can tell what wood something's made of by knocking on it. Knock on this desk. That's pine. Cheap pine.
Our house is made of stone by the quarry. It stays cool in summer, and you can hear the quarry bell at noon.
There's a spider on our family cloth. Other kids think it's scary. I pat it for luck before every test.
On clan day we all twist the rope for the shrine. My strand is in there somewhere. I'm part of the rope now.
I keep a stone from the quarry on my windowsill. My grandma says it reminds you where you stand.
Our house is next to the hospital gardens. There are drying racks on every fence and it smells like tea.
My grandma makes us drink bitter tea on clan day. I held my nose and drank it all in one go. Then I made a face.
I know the names of twenty plants already. The dangerous ones have red labels, so I stay away from red labels.
I never get sick. My mum says it's because of the bitter tea. I think it's because I eat a lot of melon bread.
My family works at night, so breakfast at our house is at sunset. I eat two breakfasts on school days.
Our house is really quiet because the walls are padded. I can practise shouting in my room and nobody hears.
On clan day we help light every lantern in the village. I lit three this year. I got to stay up so late.
My grandpa can walk across our kitchen and you'd never know. He scares me on purpose sometimes. It's a game.
My parents run the bathhouse. I know how to light the boiler. Well, I know how to watch someone light the boiler.
Everybody in my family is a farmer. I'm the first one at the Academy. My grandpa gave me a turnip for luck.
My dad's a cobbler. Every kid in my class has a sandal he fixed. I can tell which ones.
My mum's a tailor, so my clothes always fit perfectly. Except when I grow. Then she sighs.
My family makes tofu. I get up at four to help, and then I come to the Academy and fall asleep on my scroll.
My uncle is the ferryman. I've been on the boat more times than anyone in the class. I've never fallen in. Once.
My parents don't know anything about chakra, so I explain it to them at dinner. They nod a lot.
We live by the river and I can catch fish with a net. Not with my hands, that's for ninja.
I help at my family's noodle stall on weekends. I'm allowed to put the scallions on. I put on a lot of scallions.
My mum's a Chunin and she's never home on time. I don't mind. She always brings me something from the mission.
My dad's a Jonin. When he comes home he sleeps for a whole day. I put a blanket on him and tiptoe.
Both my parents are ninja. Our house has more kunai than spoons. We eat with chopsticks, mostly.
My big sister's squad came round for dinner. They ate everything. Even the vegetables. Ninja are very hungry.
My parents taught me the Rat sign before I could walk. That's what my mum says. I don't remember.
When my dad goes on a long mission I sleep in his chair. It smells like him and the forest.
The gutters on our street are rivers today! I raced two leaves down them and the green one won.
Rainy days at the Academy we practise indoors. Everyone throws practice shuriken at the cushions. The cushions lose.
My umbrella has a frog face on it. The frog is happy in the rain. So am I.
I've got mud up to my knees. My mum is going to say my name in the long way.
The rain makes the Hokage faces look like they're crying. Or washing. I think washing.
Snowball fight in the yard at recess! The Academy against the whole world!
I made a snow ninken outside our house. It has pebble eyes and a stick tail. It's guarding the door.
The ice on the Academy pond is thick enough to slide on! We're not allowed. We slid on it anyway.
My breath looks like a dragon's smoke today. I'm pretending I can do a fire jutsu.
I tried to tree-walk up a snowy tree and slid all the way down. It was the best fall I've ever had.
I counted to six between the flash and the boom. That means it's six somethings away. Six far things.
My pup hid under my bed during the storm, so I hid under the bed too, to keep it company.
The thunder made the whole classroom jump. Even the instructor jumped. Just a little.
I like watching lightning from the window. Each one is like the sky doing a jutsu.
It's so hot the cicadas are screaming. I put my feet in the water barrel at the training grounds and it was heaven.
The sky is so blue today you could swim in it. If you could swim upwards. I'm working on that.
It's windy enough to fly kites! Mine's a fish. It's stuck in the Academy tree again, but it's flying in the tree.
The cherry blossoms are falling like snow. I've got petals in my hair and my lunch and my sandals.
Spring means the frogs are back in the pond. I've counted eight. One is enormous.
My grandma is planting the garden and I'm in charge of the seeds. I've only eaten two.
It's so hot that I eat shaved ice every day. Plum one day, melon the next. Today was both.
Summer festival is coming! I'm going to catch a goldfish this year. I've been practising with a sieve.
The cicadas are so loud I can't hear the instructor. That's my excuse, anyway.
I jumped in a pile of leaves the gardener made at the Academy. Then I had to help make it again.
Roasted chestnuts are back on the corner! They're hot enough to burn your fingers and I don't care.
The maples on the Rock are all red. It looks like the Hokage faces are wearing hats made of fire.
At New Year I'm going to ring the shrine bell. I've been practising my ringing arm all week.
My hands are so cold I can't do the Tiger sign. My fingers just make the Snowman sign.
Our house has a kotatsu and I'm never coming out from under it. Except for the Academy. And dango.
I'm up before the Academy bell so I can see the sun hit the Hokage faces. The first face goes gold first.
I'm so sleepy. My brother practised hand signs in his sleep and kept poking me all night.
The bakery smells come out at this time. If you walk slowly past it, you can breakfast on smell.
Lessons are over! Now it's the best part of the day: dango, games, and nobody telling me to sit still.
I've got all afternoon and nothing to do. That means I've got all afternoon to do everything.
The dango stall is so busy after lessons. I've been in the queue so long I've grown.
The lanterns are coming on. That means I've got until the last one is lit to get home.
I can smell grilled fish from every house on our street. Mine better be fish too.
I'm meant to be going home, but the sunset is doing the orange thing on the Rock. One more minute.
I'm not supposed to be out this late. I'm just going home. Very slowly. Pretending I'm on a night mission.
My mum will be so cross. I lost track of time watching the Tobari light the lanterns on the wall.
I can't sleep, so I came out to look at the stars. I found one that looks like a shuriken.
The third target post leans because somebody hit it so hard last year. Everyone says it was a Jonin. It was a kid.
The swing's free! Quick, before the older class gets out!
The janitor keeps a jar of lost things in the office. There's a whole marble collection in it. One of them is mine.
The fish stall cat steals a sardine every day at the same time. I've been watching. It's very professional.
I love the market on Market Day. Free samples at every stall if you look hungry. I always look hungry.
The pickle lady gives you a slice if you can say all the pickles' names. I know nine.
I'm trying to skip a stone across the whole river. I got seven skips! Then it sank. Brave stone.
The herons stand so still. I tried standing like a heron and fell over in the shallows.
The ferryman lets me sit at the front of the boat sometimes. I pretend I'm captain of the Leaf's navy.
The Genin are training at Ground Three! If you lie in the grass by the stumps they don't see you. Probably.
I tried to climb the cliff like the Genin do. I got as high as my own head. It's a start.
There's an unbeatable post here. I kicked it. It's still unbeatable. My foot is beaten.
I climbed all the stairs up the Rock! My legs are jelly but I can see my house from here. It's tiny!
From up here the whole village looks like a toy. I want to pick up the Academy and shake it.
I wrote a wish plaque. I'm not telling you what it says. Okay, it says ninken. Don't tell.
The fox statues are wearing new knitted hats. I think the priest made them. The foxes look pleased.
I'm only here to visit my uncle. I'm not scared. I'm just holding the door handle very tightly.
The nurse gave me a sweet for sitting still. I've sat very still three times now. I have three sweets.
I like watching the carts come in through the gate. Today one was full of watermelons! A whole cart!
The gate guards let me sit in the booth for a minute once. There's a kettle and a book and a cushion. It's like a tiny house.
The kid upstairs practises jutsu at night. Thump, thump, and then a crash. I think they're getting better.
We play on the roof of our block where the laundry is. The sheets make the best hiding places.
Are you in the Academy too? Which class? Is your instructor the strict one or the really strict one?
Graduation is so far away. Do you think we'll both make Genin at the same time? We should.
Want to practise the Clone together after lessons? I'll be the target. Just don't throw anything.
I saw you at the target posts. You're getting better! You hit the post at least twice. I counted.
When we graduate, we'll get real headbands. I'm going to wear mine to bed.
A new Genin! I saw you come out of the Residence with your squad! What was the mission? Was it dangerous? Was it a cat?
Can you water-walk yet? Show me at the river, please! Even just one step!
You get to go to the Mission Desk now! What's it like inside? Is there a queue? Is there a dango stall?
My big brother says the first missions are just fences and gardens. Is that true? Say it's not true.
Everyone in my class talks about you now. You're like a hero. A short hero, but still.
I'm going to work really hard and be a Genin just like you. Will you wave at me when I graduate?
Your headband looks so shiny. Do you polish it? I'd polish mine every hour.
A Chunin! A real one! Can I carry something for you? Anything! I'm very strong!
Did the exams hurt? My cousin says you have to fight in a giant arena with everybody watching. Were you scared? I'd be scared.
We had to write an essay called My Village. I wrote about Ichiraku for three pages and the gate for one line.
My homework tonight is drawing the Ox sign twenty times. My Ox looks more like a cow every time.
The instructor read my test out loud as an example. A good example! I think. Nobody laughed, so it was good.
I forgot my homework, so I told the instructor my cat ate it. I don't have a cat. I need to get a cat.
In geography we learned there are other hidden villages. I didn't know there were other villages. I thought it was just us and the bandits.
We had a pop quiz on chakra today. I wrote that chakra is like soup inside you. I got half marks.
I sit next to the kid who sneezes every morning at exactly nine. You could set the Academy bell by it.
The instructor's chalk squeaks on the last letter of every word. I can't stop hearing it now.
Writing practice is the worst. My brush keeps dripping right in the middle of my best character.
I got a red circle on my sums! A red circle means right. I've been showing everybody my circle.
We learned the names of all the Hokage today. I already knew them from the Rock, so I was the first to finish.
My scroll for history came unrolled down the stairs and rolled all the way to the front door. Everyone watched.
I fell asleep in the afternoon reading and dreamed about hand signs. I woke up doing the Boar.
The instructor says if we finish the term without anybody setting the yard on fire, we get a party. It's going to be close.
We had to bring something from home for show-and-tell. I brought my grandpa's old practice kunai. It's even more blunt than mine.
The ink stone in my desk is cracked, so all my writing comes out a bit grey. I tell people it's on purpose.
I wrote the Tiger sign so many times my wrist is tired. Then I did it with my left hand so my right hand could rest.
We're learning about the wall today. It goes all the way round! I asked if it has a door at the back. It has gates.
Our class has a pet goldfish in a bowl. Every day somebody different feeds it. It's very round now.
The old scrolls in the library have pictures of ninja with really big hair. Everybody had really big hair back then.
I got moved to the front row for talking. The front row is nice. You can see the chalk better.
Our instructor has a scar, and everybody has a different story about it. Mine's about a bear. It's the best story.
The test was so hard I chewed my brush. Now my mouth is black and my answers are still wrong.
The Academy bell is broken, so the janitor bangs a pot instead. Everyone runs when they hear the pot.
I got sent to the hall and found out the hall is actually quite peaceful. I might get sent more.
Every morning the instructor checks our headbands are tied right. Mine always falls over one eye by lunch.
We had to stand on one leg in the yard for balance practice. The kid next to me lasted the longest. I lasted the loudest.
I traded homework answers with my friend, and we both got them wrong in the exact same way. The instructor knew.
The library has a book of jokes for ninja. They're all terrible. I've memorised every one.
My practice shuriken bounced off the post and landed in the instructor's tea. That's a hit, right?
At recess we play statues. You freeze like a ninja on a mission. I can stay still until my nose itches.
We made a fort out of the gym mats. Then the instructor found it and made it a lesson about defence.
I'm the best at jacks in my class. I can pick up five at once. Six if nobody's watching.
We play Hokage says at recess. It's like the normal game but the Hokage is very bossy.
We drew a hopscotch in the yard and numbered it to twelve, one for each hand sign. You have to do the sign on every square.
Spinning tops are back! Mine is red and it wobbles, but it spins longer than anybody's.
We played catch with a rice ball by accident. It was somebody's lunch. They were not happy.
There's a game where one person is the bandit and everyone else has to sneak past. I'm always the bandit because I'm good at grumpy faces.
We had a paper plane contest off the Academy steps. Mine flew all the way to the dango stall. I went to get it, and stayed.
Rock, paper, kunai. It's like the normal one but kunai beats everything. We argue about it a lot.
I can do a handstand against the woodshed for a count of twenty. I'm working on doing it without the woodshed.
We played marbles in the dirt and I won four. Then I lost five. I'm down one marble. It was a good game.
We have a club at recess. It's called the Secret Ninja Club. Everybody knows about it. That's the only problem.
Somebody brought a skipping rope and we skipped until the bell. I did forty skips! Then I tripped on the forty-first.
We have a relay at recess where you pass a stick instead of a scroll. The stick is very important. Don't drop the stick.
We build stone towers in the yard and knock them down with practice shuriken. Building is better. Knocking down is louder.
Leapfrog over the training logs is the best game. Unless you don't jump high enough. Then it's the worst game.
We play a game where you have to cross the yard without touching the ground. Benches, logs and the janitor's cart count.
The best place to play hide-and-seek is inside the big empty barrel by the workshop. Don't tell anyone. It's my barrel.
We were playing tug-of-war with a rope and the rope broke. Both teams fell over. Everyone won.
I got ten ryo for my birthday! I'm going to spend it carefully. Three on dango. Seven on more dango.
I found a one-ryo note on the main street. I thought about it a lot and then bought a rice cracker.
My pocket money is two ryo a week. The dango stall has started saying hello to me by name.
I'm saving up for a real paper fan from the festival. It costs eight ryo. I have three and a half. I don't know where the half came from.
The sweets shop has a jar of hard candies, one ryo for three. The orange ones last the longest. I've timed them.
I helped carry crates at the grocer and got two ryo. That's the first money I ever earned. I'm keeping the note forever. Or until tomorrow.
Ichiraku's small bowl is the perfect size for a kid. I can almost finish it. Almost.
There's a bean bun stall that only opens on Market Day. The buns are as big as my face, and the beans are still warm.
I tried green tea because grown-ups drink it all the time. It tastes like a garden. I don't know why they like it.
I can eat seven dango in a row. I've never tried eight. I'm scared of what happens at eight.
The grilled corn stall by the river puts butter and soy on it. I get it all over my sleeves. My mum knows exactly where I've been.
I swapped my lunch with my friend every day this week. It turned out we both have the same lunch. We still swap.
My favourite ramen topping is the egg. I save it for the very end. If anyone touches my egg, we're enemies.
I keep a list of every snack I've tried in the village. I'm on number forty-two. Number forty-two was a weird pickle.
I spent all my money on candy and now I'm sad. But I also have candy. It's complicated.
The sweet potato man rings a little bell when he comes down our street. I can hear it from inside the house.
Ichiraku gave me extra seaweed because I said thank you so loud. Being loud works sometimes.
I tried to cook rice by myself and it came out like glue. My dad ate it anyway and said it was very sticky. Sticky is a compliment.
There's a stall that sells little fish-shaped cakes with bean paste inside. I always eat the tail first so it can't swim away.
I want to try the barbecue house so badly. Everyone who comes out of it smells amazing and looks very full.
My big brother let me wear his flak vest for one minute. It came down to my knees. I felt like a Chunin.
My mum braids my hair so tight before the Academy that my eyebrows go up. I look very surprised all day.
My little sister follows me to the Academy gate every morning and cries when I go in. Then she forgets and plays.
My dad snores like a cart going over cobbles. I can hear it from the other end of the house.
My big sister is teaching me to throw. She says I throw like I'm angry at the post. I'm not angry. I'm determined.
My mum works late and my grandma cooks dinner. Grandma's dinners are bigger. Don't tell Mum.
My twin and I swapped places at the Academy for a whole morning. Nobody noticed. The instructor noticed at lunch.
My brother and I share a room. There's a line down the middle. His side is messy. My side is slightly less messy.
My dad tells the same story about the bear every winter. The bear gets bigger every time. It's huge now.
My mum can tell if I've washed my hands by looking at my face. I don't know how. It's a mum jutsu.
My grandma has a cat that's older than me. It sleeps all day and only moves for fish.
My little brother learned to say kunai before he could say my name. I'm still a bit upset about it.
My big sister got her headband and wore it to dinner, to bed and in the bath. Mum took it off her when she was asleep.
When my parents argue, they do it in whispers. I can still hear it, but they think I can't.
My dad makes paper cranes when he's thinking. Our whole house has cranes on every shelf.
My mum sings when she cooks. She sings very badly. It's my favourite sound.
My big brother says I'm too small to understand. I'm small, but I understand everything. Mostly.
I have three older sisters and they all tell me what to do. I'm going to be Hokage just so I can tell them what to do.
My grandpa falls asleep in his chair after lunch, and I put his slippers on the wrong feet. He never notices.
I want a pet so badly I've started pretending my sandal is a dog. Its name is Sandal.
The kennels let you pet the old dogs if you're gentle. The oldest one has a grey nose and leans on your legs.
I caught a cricket and kept it in a box by my bed. It chirped all night. I let it go in the morning. I was tired.
There's a cat on the Academy wall that comes to every lesson. I think it's learning hand signs too.
I saw a hawk from the Residence fly right over the Academy. Everybody looked up. The instructor looked up too.
My goldfish is called General. General is very brave. General is a fish.
There's a tortoise at the shrine pond that's a hundred years old. I asked it questions. It didn't answer.
I found a snail on the Academy steps and carried it to the grass so nobody would step on it. It took a long time.
A dog followed me home from the market and my mum made me take it back. I walked very, very slowly.
The ducks on the river chase you if you have bread. I had bread. I ran.
There's a frog that lives in the water barrel by the Academy workshop. Every time you open it, the frog looks offended.
I'm training an ant colony. Well, I'm feeding them crumbs and they're doing what they want. That's training.
I named all the pigeons on the Hokage Rock. There are too many. Now they all have the same three names.
A butterfly landed on my hand during practice and I couldn't move until it flew off. The instructor said that was the best stillness exercise all week.
They dared me to eat a spoonful of wasabi. My nose is still on fire. I won though.
I dared my friend to sit on the third target post during throwing practice. The instructor dared us to stop.
The dare was to walk all the way down the main street with my eyes shut. I made it to the tailor's before I walked into a pole.
I dared someone to say the twelve hand signs backwards really fast. They did it! I'm still practising.
Somebody dared me to climb into the empty water tank on our roof. It echoed when I shouted. Best dare ever.
The dare was to touch the Inuzuka gate and run before the dogs barked. The dogs barked before I even got there.
I got dared to ask the bath house keeper for a bath in my clothes. I didn't do it. That's a dare for older kids.
I dared my little brother to eat a whole lemon. He did it and then cried. I bought him a dango to say sorry.
The double dare is jumping off the second step of the Academy stairs. The triple dare is the third step. Nobody's done the triple.
I dared everyone to stay quiet for a whole minute at lunch. We lasted ten seconds. Somebody burped.
They dared me to knock on the door of the empty house on our lane. I knocked and a cat came out. I screamed. The cat screamed too.
The scariest dare is running round the shrine three times at night. I've done it once. My legs ran faster than me.
My friend says if you whisper your name to the Hokage Rock, one of the faces winks at you. I've tried six times.
Everyone says the janitor used to be a famous Jonin. I watched how they sweep. It does look a bit like sword fighting.
There's a rumour that Ichiraku's broth has a secret ingredient that makes you faster. I had two bowls and ran home. It was true.
A kid in the year above says if you sleep with a kunai under your pillow you dream of missions. I tried with a spoon. I dreamed of soup.
Somebody said there's a giant fish in the river as big as a boat. I've been looking every day. I've seen a big log.
My cousin says the instructor can see through walls. That's why I always sit up straight, even in the toilet.
People say the oldest tree in the village grew from a single seed the first Hokage planted. I've been planting seeds everywhere just in case.
My friend says if you can catch a falling cherry petal, you'll make Genin first try. I caught four.
There's a story that the bathhouse mural changes when nobody's looking. I stared at it for an hour. It didn't change. My eyes did.
Everyone says the dango maker can make a fourth colour if you ask nicely. I asked. It was purple. It tasted bruised.
Somebody told me that if you count all the lanterns on the main street you get a wish. I lost count at fifty-three.
The big kids say the cliff at the training grounds has a ninja's footprint at the very top. Nobody can get up to check.
When I'm a ninja I'm going to have a cool cloak that flaps in the wind. Even when there's no wind.
I practise my mission face in the mirror. Serious, eyebrows down, mouth straight. Then I laugh and have to start again.
In my daydreams I'm the one who saves the whole village from a dragon. Then everyone buys me ramen.
I'm going to have a signature move. I've decided on a spinning kick. I just need to stop falling over after the spin.
When I graduate I'll jump from roof to roof all the way to the Academy, and wave at everyone below.
I'm going to be so fast that people only see a blur and then a puff of dust. And then me, waving.
I'm inventing a jutsu where you turn into a cloud and float wherever you want. The hand signs are very complicated.
In my head I'm already a Jonin. The real me just has to catch up.
If I had my own squad, we'd have matching scarves. Red ones. And a motto. I haven't thought of the motto yet.
When I'm famous my face will go on the Rock, and I'll make sure they carve my best side.
I want a summoning animal so badly. I'd pick a giant owl, so I could fly home at night.
I'm going to be the first ninja who can do hand signs with their toes. I practise in the bath.
Sometimes I pretend my walk to the Academy is an escort mission and my lunch box is the client.
I've decided my ninja name will be Shadow Wind. My mum says I already have a name. That's my civilian name.
When I'm a ninja, I'll come back to the Academy and show all the little kids how to throw. And I'll be really nice about it.
I scraped my knee on the Academy steps. It's got a scab shaped like the Leaf symbol. I'm keeping it as long as I can.
I fell off the swing and landed on my elbow. It's purple and green now. Everyone wants to look at it.
I got a splinter from the training log. My mum took it out with a needle and I only yelled a little.
I've got a bandage on my chin from falling over my own shadow. That's what I'm telling people. Really I tripped on a cat.
My knee bled through my trousers, but I finished the race anyway. The instructor gave me a nod. A real nod!
I bumped my head on the low beam in the workshop. Now I have a lump. My friend calls it my second brain.
I bit my tongue eating crackers too fast. Now everything tastes like a coin.
I've had four plasters this week. My mum says she's going to buy them by the box.
I sprained my finger doing the Boar sign wrong. Is that even possible? It is. I did it.
My hands are all blisters from swinging on the bar. The instructor says that means I'm getting stronger. They also hurt.
When I fall over, I count to three and get up. If I'm still sad at three, I count to ten.
I cut my thumb on a sheet of paper in the library. The library lady gave me a sweet. I'm going to be more careful. Or less.
The festival is coming! I've been practising goldfish scooping in the bath with a ladle and some pebbles.
I'm wearing a yukata to the festival this year. It's blue with white rabbits. My mum says I can't run in it. I'm going to try.
At the festival there's a candy apple stall that does the apples in red sugar. I'm going to get one and not share it.
Fireworks are my favourite part of the festival. I lie on the grass and watch them, and the sky goes boom inside my chest.
I want to win a prize at the ring toss this year. There's a stuffed ninken on the top shelf, and I want it.
At New Year you get money in a little envelope. I'm saving mine for the summer festival. That's planning.
I'm going to make my own lantern for the festival. It'll be shaped like a fish. Right now it's shaped like a squashed fish.
The festival masks are the best. I'm getting the fox one this year. Last year I got the frog and nobody knew who I was.
Before the festival everybody hangs paper lanterns across the street. I helped tie one up. It's the crooked one.
There's a game at the festival where you shoot corks at prizes. I knocked a box over last year. The box was empty.
On festival night I get to stay up until the fireworks finish. It's the latest I ever stay up. I'm always so tired and so happy.
I'm counting down the days until the festival on the kitchen wall. My dad keeps rubbing out the days to tease me.
The shrine has a festival with drums. When the drums go, the ground shakes and my heart beats the same.
At New Year I'm going to wish for a ninken and a passing mark and a really big bowl of ramen. In that order.
I can see the Hokage faces from my bedroom window. I say goodnight to each one before I go to sleep.
The second face on the Rock looks like it's about to sneeze. Once you see it, you can't stop seeing it.
I want to climb up the Rock and sit on top of a face. Just for a minute. I'd be very respectful.
When it's sunny the faces look happy. When it's cloudy they look like they're thinking about homework.
The fourth face is my favourite. It looks like it knows a joke and won't tell anyone.
I drew the Rock in art class and gave all the faces hats. The instructor said it was creative. That means good, I think.
There's a space on the Rock for more faces. I measured it with my thumb. Mine would fit.
At sunset the faces go orange. My grandpa says that's when the Hokage are proudest of the village.
I wonder if the Hokage get embarrassed about their faces being so big. I'd be embarrassed. And also very happy.
Birds sit on the noses of the faces. I think that would tickle if they were real.
From the market street you can see the faces between the roofs. They're always watching. In a nice way.
Ichiraku has a stool that spins a little. If you sit there, you can turn round to see who's coming in.
I watched the cook at Ichiraku pull noodles. They stretched and stretched and never broke. It's a jutsu, I'm sure.
The steam from the ramen counter makes my face all warm and my nose run. It's the best feeling.
I can slurp noodles louder than anyone in my class. At Ichiraku slurping is polite, so I'm the most polite.
Ichiraku's lantern is the first one on the street to light up. I race it home every evening.
I want to eat at Ichiraku every day when I'm a Genin. I'll have to do a lot of missions to pay for it.
There's a picture on the wall at Ichiraku of a ninja eating ramen. I asked who it was and the cook just smiled.
The best thing at Ichiraku is when they give you a bowl and the egg is perfect. Gold in the middle. Wobbly.
I saved for two weeks to have a whole bowl at Ichiraku with my friend. We counted our coins on the counter. The cook waited.
When it rains, everyone squeezes onto the stools at Ichiraku and there's no room for elbows. I love it.
I don't like the dark in my room. The coat on the hook looks like a bandit. I put it in the cupboard every night.
I sleep with a little lamp on. My brother calls me a baby. He sleeps with a lamp too, I've seen it.
When I walk home after dark I run past the alley by the tea house. Nothing's ever been there. I still run.
My mum says the dark is just the day with its eyes closed. That helps a bit.
I'm not scared of the dark. I'm scared of what's in the dark. Which is nothing. Probably.
At night the wind makes the shutters creak like footsteps. I pretend it's a Tobari watchman walking by. That makes it better.
The stairs in our house creak on the fourth step. When I hear it at night, I know it's just my dad getting water.
I hide under my blanket when I hear owls. Owls sound like ghosts. They're just birds. Big ghost birds.
I count the lanterns on the wall from my window when I can't sleep. If they're all lit, the village is safe.
When the lamp goes out at night I say every hand sign in my head. By the Dog I'm usually asleep.
I collect bottle caps. I have thirty-one. The gold one is from the tea house and it's my best one.
I've got a box of feathers under my bed. Crow, pigeon, duck and one blue one I can't name. I think it's a magic bird.
I collect smooth stones from the river. I only keep the ones that feel warm in your hand. Those are the lucky ones.
I'm collecting all the different festival masks. I have three. The frog, the cat and one with a broken nose.
I keep every wrapper from every sweet I've ever eaten. My mum says it's rubbish. It's a history.
